summary: Task 4's TelegramSender implementation meets all focus-area requirements. A02 (crypto): plaintext token lives only inside the Mono closure for at most the 30s overall timeout, is never logged/serialized/persisted, and the narrow Base64 catch (TelegramSender.java:140-146) correctly translates only IllegalArgumentException to a 422 BotTokenInvalidException — IllegalStateException from AEAD-tag failure / misconfigured TokenEncryptor bean propagates as 500 per Risk R7 and is verified by `sendText_decryptThrowsIllegalState_propagatesAsInternalError_notBotTokenInvalid` (TelegramSenderTest.java:514-538). A03 (injection): URI is built via `webClient.post().uri("/bot{token}/sendMessage", token)` with `DefaultUriBuilderFactory.EncodingMode.NONE`, but `TelegramApiClient.requireValidTokenShape` (TelegramSender.java:153) constrains the token to `\d{1,20}:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,50}` — all URL-safe — before substitution, so path injection is impossible; `parse_mode` defaults to null and the body is only added when explicitly provided. A09 (logging): all six scrub sites route through `TelegramApiClient.scrubTokens(...)` — line 129 (terminal error), line 199 (429 warn with retry_after), line 202 (4xx warn), line 216 (ok=false warn), line 235 (transient retry warn); line 247's 429-wait log only emits the int delay and jitter so it has no leak surface. Five token-leak tests (TelegramSenderTest.java:622-720) cover 4xx descriptions, 5xx retry logs, 429 retry logs, terminal-failure error logs, and the transport-error path with token-bearing URI. A01 (access control): both `findById → Mono.empty()` and `bot.status != CONNECTED` collapse to the identical 404 with `MESSAGE_BOT_NOT_FOUND` (TelegramSender.java:113-115), and the two scenarios are verified by `sendText_botNotFound_throwsNotFound_noHttp` and `sendText_botDisconnected_throwsNotFound_noHttp` — no oracle for system-context callers. Audit metadata: `sentMetadata` (botId/chatId/messageId) and `failedMetadata` (botId/chatId/attempts/errorCode/errorDescription) never carry token-shaped data — `errorDescription` is `TelegramSendException.getMessage()` which is the already-scrubbed description set by `toThrowable` / `mapBodyToSentMessage`, and the `"transient_failure_exhausted"` / `"timeout"` constants contain no secrets. `TelegramSendException` extends `AppException`, so `GlobalErrorHandler.handleAppException` returns the scrubbed message in response bodies — safe. `TelegramRateLimitException` is package-private, carries only an int retryAfter, and is filtered into the rate-limit retry loop (never escapes to GlobalErrorHandler in normal flow); if it did escape, it would hit `handleThrowable` and return a generic 500. IT fixtures use `Zm9v`/`YmFy` (Base64 for foo/bar) — not real credentials. No hardcoded secrets found in the three changed files. No SSRF surface (token is the only path component substituted, validated to a fixed shape, base URL is config-injected via `app.telegram.base-url`). No deserialization risk (Jackson reads typed `TelegramSendResult<JsonNode>` from controlled Telegram responses). No dependency or component changes.
